sections.title: Identification
sections.text: Clitocybe odora remains widely used in field guides; a 2023 phylogenomic study proposed the combination Collybia odora. The cap, usually 3–8 cm across, is initially convex, then flattens and may become depressed at the centre. Its matte surface is blue-green to grey-green, often fading towards grey or cream with age or in dry weather. The young margin is incurved and may become wavy.

sections.title: Gills and stem
sections.text: The gills are pale, cream to faintly greenish, fairly broad and moderately spaced; they are adnate to slightly decurrent. The stem is fibrous, often somewhat curved, usually paler than the cap and sometimes widened towards the base; it may become hollow with age. The base often bears white mycelial felt. There is no ring or volva.

sections.title: Odour, habitat and season
sections.text: The anise-like odour is strong and characteristic, especially in fresh specimens. It grows on the ground among forest litter, mostly in broadleaf woodland, but also in mixed woods and sometimes under conifers. It is mainly recorded in summer and autumn; the precise season varies with climate and region.

sections.title: Taxonomy and safety
sections.text: Collybia odora (Bull.) Z.M. He & Zhu L. Yang is the combination proposed in 2023; Clitocybe odora (Bull.) P. Kumm. is the historical name and remains common in the literature. The DGfM and VAPKO lists classify it as edible, though its powerful anise flavour is not liked by everyone. A 2023 study did not detect muscarine in the basidiomes it analysed; this limited result does not guarantee every collection or identify a mushroom from a photo. Pale clitocybes can be difficult to distinguish: do not eat any wild mushroom without secure expert identification.

traits: Matte blue-green to grey-green cap, often fading to grey or cream; margin initially incurved, sometimes becoming wavy
Pale, fairly broad and moderately spaced gills, adnate to slightly decurrent
Fibrous, pale stem, often curved or broadened at the base, sometimes hollow with age; no ring or volva
Strong anise-like odour in fresh specimens
On woodland litter, mostly under broadleaf trees, sometimes in mixed woods or under conifers; mainly summer and autumn
safetyNote: Listed as edible by DGfM and VAPKO, but its powerful anise aroma is a culinary preference, not an identification test. A study reported no muscarine in the specimens it analysed; do not extrapolate that result to every collection. Never eat a wild mushroom identified only from an image.
